MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  JUNE 27, 2017

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
City Council Member Absent:  Mitchell

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Deputy City Attorney Kane Thuyen
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton

Others Present:  Jeff Romanelli, Park and Activities Commission

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

A representative from Boy Scout Troop 783 led the audience in the Pledge of Allegiance.

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

  NONE

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  ADJOURNED BUDGET STUDY SESSION MINUTES OF JUNE 6, 2017

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO APPROVE THE ADJOURNED BUDGET STUDY SESSION MINUTES
  OF JUNE 6, 2017 AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JUNE 13, 2017

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JUNE 13, 2017 AS
  PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS - JUNE

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 58536 THROUGH 58573 FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $187,589.54 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
JUNE 27, 2017
 6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A-D.

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to
  the City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be
  read by title only.

  APPROVED.

B.  MAY 2017 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

C.  MAY MONTHLY REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  CITY CREDIT CARD POLICY AND PROCEDURES

  RECEIVED AND FILED THE CITY CREDIT CARD POLICY, CREDIT CARD
  USER AGREEMENT AND LIST OF AUTHORIZED CREDIT CARD USERS.

E.  SEMI-ANNUAL CODE ENFORCEMENT REPORT

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN inquired about two properties that were not on the list.
  Code Administrator Slawson responded that her report only highlighted major
  violations. MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that he will provide the information for
  Code Administrator Slawson to follow up.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF commented that she has received complaints
  regarding gardeners beginning work before the approved hours.  Code
  Administrator Slawson noted that the Sheriff’s Department should be notified
  and to obtain a tag number so the violation can be addressed. She encouraged
  the homeowners’ associations to remind property owners regarding the hours of
  operation.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE SEMI-ANNUAL CODE ENFORCEMENT
  REPORT.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

7.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

  NONE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JUNE 27, 2017
 9.  NEW BUSINESS (Taken out of order)

A.  ADJOURNED PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF JUNE 19,
  2017

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF JUNE 19, 2017.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

B.  DESIGNATION OF CITY’S AGENTS BY TITLE TO OBTAIN FEDERAL AND/OR
  STATE FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE THROUGH THE CALIFORNIA OFFICE OF
  EMERGENCY SERVICES

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Designation of Applicant's
  Agent Resolution for Non-State Agencies designating Assistant City Manager,
  Assistant to the City Manager, and Code Administrator/Planning Technician as
  authorized agents.

  Code Administrator Slawson provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE DESIGNATION OF APPLICANT’S AGENT
  RESOLUTION FOR NON-STATE AGENCIES DESIGNATING ASSISTANT
  CITY MANAGER, ASSISTANT TO THE CITY MANAGER, AND CODE
  ADMINISTRATOR/PLANNING TECHNICIAN AS AUTHORIZED AGENTS
  AND ADOPTED RESOLUTION NO. 2400.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  AWARD OF BID – EQUESTRIAN CROSSINGS WITH IN-ROADWAY WARNING
  LIGHTS ON ROLLING HILLS ROAD AND PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH

  Recommendation: That the City Council award the bid in the amount of
  $148,362 to California Professional Engineering, Inc., for the Rectangular Rapid
  Flashing Beacon (RRFB) and In-Roadway Warning Lights (IRWL) Installation
  Project for equestrian crossings at Rolling Hills Road and Palomino Ranchos
  Trail and at Palos Verdes Drive North and 3739 Palos Verdes Drive North.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ regarding the cost, Assistant City
  Manager Grammer noted that many contractors considered this too small a
  project.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF

  TO AWARD THE BID IN THE AMOUNT OF $148,362 TO CALIFORNIA
  PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING, INC., FOR THE RECTANGULAR RAPID
  FLASHING BEACON (RRFB) AND IN-ROADWAY WARNING LIGHTS (IRWL)
  INSTALLATION PROJECT FOR EQUESTRIAN CROSSINGS AT ROLLING
  HILLS ROAD AND PALOMINO RANCHOS TRAIL AND AT PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE NORTH AND 3739 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JUNE 27, 2017
   COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN inquired if the contract should include language to
  begin before school starts. Assistant City Manager Grammer noted that the work
  should happen shortly before the school year starts and in any event work hours
  are limited.

B.  ORDINANCE NO. 719 FOR SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES AMENDING AND RESTATING CHAPTER 5.04 OF THE ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO BUSINESS LICENSING

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 719.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

  City Manager Prichard read Ordinance No. 719 by title only.

C.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 15-17 LOS ANGELES COMMUNITY CHOICE
  ENERGY (LACCE) ENABLING ORDINANCE AND JOINT POWERS AUTHORITY
  ADOPTION; LOCATION: CITY-WIDE

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Approve for second reading and
  adopt Ordinance No. 718 approving the Joint Powers Agreement for Los Angeles
  Community Choice Energy and Authorizing the Implementation of a
  Community Choice Aggregation Program; and 2) Designate one regular Director
  who will be authorized to act on behalf of the City on matters within the powers
  of the Authority, as well as appoint up to two alternate Directors, who may vote
  on matters when the regular Director is absent from a Board meeting.

  Senior Planner Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  After brief discussion, COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR
  PRO TEM HUFF

  TO: 1) ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 718 APPROVING THE JOINT POWERS
  AGREEMENT FOR LOS ANGELES COMMUNITY CHOICE ENERGY AND
  AUTHORIZING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF A COMMUNITY CHOICE
  AGGREGATION PROGRAM; AND 2) DESIGNATE COUNCILMAN
  ZUCKERMAN WHO WILL BE AUTHORIZED TO ACT ON BEHALF OF THE
  CITY ON MATTERS WITHIN THE POWERS OF THE AUTHORITY, AS WELL
  AS APPOINT COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL AND SENIOR PLANNER
  NAUGHTON TO ACT AS THE ALTERNATE DIRECTORS WHO MAY VOTE
  ON MATTERS WHEN THE REGULAR DIRECTOR IS ABSENT FROM A
  BOARD MEETING.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. by title only.

D.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 18-16; APPROVAL OF CONTRACT WITH ACCESS
  PACIFIC, INC. FOR STORM DRAIN IMPROVEMENTS ON JUNE’S TRAIL AT
  PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize staff to enter into a contract
  with Access Pacific Incorporated, in the amount of $277,499.30 plus a 5%
  contingency for potential cost overruns of $13,875; and, a contract with
  Transtech Engineering in the amount of $13,300, for project construction
  management services, for a grand total of $304,674.30 for "Storm Drain
  Improvements on June's Trail," a public works project.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JUNE 27, 2017
   COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN inquired about references for Access Pacific, and if
  they have experience with this type of work.  Tom Ragland, Transtech
  Engineering, stated that the Axiom Group will subcontract the concrete
  structures.

  In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN, Mr. Ragland noted that they will
  have an inspector on site periodically.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, Planning Director Wahba noted
  that additional Quimby funds will be coming in during FY2018-19.

  Brief discussion continued regarding the 5% contingency. COUNCILWOMAN
  SCHMITZ inquired if this amount provided enough of a cushion. Planning
  Director Wahba responded that this project is unique and has a lot of moving
  parts, but will look into the possibility of increasing the contingency. City
  Manager Prichard noted that if an increase is warranted, he can be authorized
  to act on the COUNCIL’S behalf.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN thanked Transtech and the Dapplegray Homeowners’
  representative for attending the meeting noting this has been an issue for a long
  time in his neighborhood. He further noted that the trail is needed for those
  property owners who have this area as their only access.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO AUTHORIZE STAFF TO ENTER INTO A CONTRACT WITH ACCESS
  PACIFIC INCORPORATED, IN THE AMOUNT OF $277,499.30 PLUS 5%
  CONTINGENCY FOR POTENTIAL COST OVERRUNS OF $13,875; AND
  ENTER INTO A CONTRACT WITH TRANSTECH ENGINEERING IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $13,300, FOR PROJECT CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT
  SERVICES, FOR A GRAND TOTAL OF $304,674.30 FOR “STORM DRAIN
  IMPROVEMENTS ON JUNE’S TRAIL,” A PUBLIC WORKS PROJECT.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

E.  ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING STATION AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the contract with Voltaic for
  a dual port electric vehicle charging station to be installed at City Hall in the
  amount of $18,857.96.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ inquired as to how the parking lot pavement would
  be affected. Assistant to the City Manager Davis noted that it should not have
  much of an impact, but restriping would be necessary.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, Administrative Services Director
  Whitehead noted the cost of restriping would be minimal.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO AUTHORIZE THE CONTRACT WITH VOLTAIC FOR A DUAL PORT
  ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING STATION TO BE INSTALLED AT CITY
  HALL IN THE AMOUNT OF $22,770.76 AS AMENDED.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JUNE 27, 2017
 8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

A.  FY 2017-18 BUDGET PUBLIC HEARING AND ADOPTION

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the public hearing and take
  any public testimony related to the budget adoption, including fees and
  charges, fund balance policy, and investment policy; 2) Close the public
  hearing; and 3) Review and adopt Resolution Nos. 2397, 2398, and 2399,
  Statement of Fund Balance Policy, and Statement of Investment Policy.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per
  agenda material).

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN commended staff on a job well done and noted that the
  budget is available on the City’s website and encouraged everyone to read this
  information. He then provided an extensive explanation of the budget for the
  audience. Finally, he reported that the City received the Government Finance
  Officers Association Award of Excellence for the most recent Comprehensive
  Annual Financial Report.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

  No public testimony was offered.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZERUNYAN SO ORDERED.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN

  TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2397 ADOPTING THE CONSOLIDATED
  BUDGET FOR THE FISCAL YEAR 2017-18 MAKING APPROPRIATIONS
  THERETO AND AUTHORIZING EXPENDITURES THEREFROM.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. 2397 by title only.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2398 ESTABLISHING THE 2017-18
  FISCAL YEAR APPROPRIATION LIMIT FOR THE CITY OF ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES AND SELECT THE CHANGE IN CALIFORNIA PER CAPITA
  PERSONAL INCOME AS THE INFLATION FACTOR FOR THE FISCAL YEAR
  2017-18 AND SELECT THE GROWTH OF THE COUNTY AS THE
  POPULATION FACTOR FOR FISCAL YEAR 2017-18.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. 2398 by title only.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
JUNE 27, 2017
   MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2399 ESTABLISHING A COMPREHENSIVE
  SCHEDULE OF MUNICIPAL FEES AND CHARGES FOR THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2017-18, THE FUND BALANCE POLICY, AND INVESTMENT
  POLICY.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. 2399 by title only.

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

  NONE

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of
  currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and
  their various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or
  have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.
